Segregation transport¶

The segregation operator transports grain fractions while preserving each mobile species mass and each particle’s total mass. Rigid materials do not participate. Enable it with segregate=True and supply grain diameters, composition, and the model coefficients described in the tutorial.

For species k, the conserved inventory is

Q[k] = sum_p m[p] phi[p,k] = sum_i M[i] phi_grid[i,k]

Periodic endpoint duplicates count once. Because nodal masses can differ, conserving an unweighted sum of concentration increments is insufficient. Both weighted species conservation and local mixture closure sum_k phi[k]=1 are required.

Grid flux and mass exchanges¶

The relative concentration flux uses segregation and diffusion coefficients:

F[k] = c*phi[k]*(1/(s[k]*sum_j(phi[j]/s[j])) - 1)*grad(pk)
       - D*grad(phi[k])

A scalar limiter is shared across the whole reconstructed mixture. Both sides of a face use one common numerical speed, bounded by the advective Jacobian row norm. Physical diffusion uses the cell-centre concentration difference separately from advection and numerical stabilisation. These choices preserve zero total relative mixture flux without selecting a special dependent grain class.

Each face exchanges a species-mass vector T[k], rather than evolving an unweighted concentration. Flux density uses the harmonic mean of adjacent mobile mass densities, M[i]/V[i], and the face’s actual area. Boundary control volumes have half widths. Closed boundaries block exterior faces; empty nodes and internal walls block transport through their normal faces. Periodic faces are evaluated once, then copied to the display endpoint.

The same T[k] is removed from one node and added to its neighbour. Thus each species is globally conservative. Concentration increments are obtained by dividing the resulting nodal mass increments by the participating nodal mass. Rigid particles are excluded from both the transport inventory and the return transfer.

Bounded return to particles¶

The return transfer uses actual species inventories so depleted classes cannot supply grains they do not own, and diffusion can mix pure layers.

For a face carrying class k from node i, its donor weights are

donor[p,i,k] = m[p]*N[p,i]*phi[p,k] / Q[i,k]

where Q[i,k] is the deposited mobile species mass. A donor particle loses only grains it owns and receives equal mass from the counter-flowing classes on that face. Each particle’s total mass stays fixed, and the opposite side receives the same species masses. For uniform composition this reduces to an incremental concentration gather. When physical and numerical fluxes are zero, particle composition is unchanged: there is no unconditional PIC smoothing.

Outgoing demand is budgeted over all faces in both directions before updating. One factor per face limits every class together, so limiting preserves both species conservation and zero mixture flux. A small floating-point balance of oppositely signed face totals precedes the return transfer. Fractions are never clipped or renormalised by this algorithm.

The grid API is G.calculate_phi_increment(P, L) for the coupled update. It stages both G.dphi and inventory-aware particle increments. The main timestep and benchmark driver pass L. Calling it without L, or calling increment_grainsize(P, G), returns the standalone grid update; its caller is responsible for its explicit timestep stability.

Verification¶

Checks include nonuniform nodal/particle masses, local fraction sums, coupled species inventories, rigid particles, free surfaces, closed and periodic faces, class-order permutation, both spatial directions, pure-layer mixing, and transport steps far beyond the unbounded explicit update. A node-aligned sinusoidal mixture reproduces the discrete heat-equation step for constant diffusivity. The slope examples also run for 1,000 steps with normalisation off.

Measurements and environment information are in benchmarks/segregation_drift.json. Reproduce them with python -m benchmarks.segregation_drift --output /tmp/poly-mpm-segregation.json. The benchmark guide distinguishes report configurations.

These checks establish conservation, bounds, and specific diffusion behaviour; they do not validate the segregation constitutive law against experiments. The diffusion coefficient has a special zero-inertial-number convention. Limiting can reduce transport when particle inventories cannot supply a proposed exchange, so quantitative predictions still require mesh/timestep convergence checks.

The central-upwind framework and its reconstruction/flux distinction are described by Kurganov and Lin (2007).

poly-mpm
